rounds.text: Granules India demonstrates significant operational momentum, evidenced by a 25% compounded sales growth and 36% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21]. This performance is supported by a clear expansion in profitability, with operating margins rising by 4 percentage points over the last three years and maintaining a strong 23% level [E30]. The company’s efficiency is superior to its sector peers, as shown by an ROA of 8.58% and ROCE of 13.63%, both of which outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E10]. Furthermore, the business is generating high-quality earnings, with cash conversion at 1.33x and operating cash flow reaching Rs 793 Cr, ensuring that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34, E35]. Institutional confidence is shifting, as evidenced by domestic institutions increasing their stake by 9.05 percentage points and a positive money flow signal [E44, E45]. Conceded: the stock trades at a premium valuation with a P/B of 4.44x against a sector benchmark of 2.95x, and the DCF model suggests the current price reflects aggressive growth expectations [E7, E46, E48].

Granules India is currently demonstrating a powerful inflection in operational performance, evidenced by a 25% compounded sales growth and a 36% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21]. This momentum is supported by a significant expansion in profitability, with operating margins rising by 4 percentage points over the last three years [E30]. The company’s efficiency is superior to its peers, as shown by an ROA of 8.58% and an ROCE of 13.63%, both of which comfortably outpace sector benchmarks [E8, E10]. Furthermore, the business is generating high-quality earnings, with a cash conversion ratio of 1.33x and operating cash flow of Rs 793 Cr, ensuring that profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34, E35]. Institutional confidence is clearly shifting, as evidenced by a 9.05 percentage point increase in domestic institutional holdings and a positive money flow signal [E44, E45]. Conceded: the stock trades at a premium valuation with a P/B of 4.44x against a sector benchmark of 2.95x, and the DCF model suggests the current price is significantly ahead of intrinsic value [E7, E46, E47]. Conceded: promoter and foreign institutional holdings have declined over the last three years [E42, E43].
